accessibility.name: Texas Accessibility Standards (TAS)
accessibility.authority: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR), Architectural Barriers program
accessibility.summary: Besides the 2010 ADA Standards, the 2012 Texas Accessibility Standards apply. Projects with a total estimated cost of $50,000 or more must be registered with TDLR and submitted for plan review; smaller projects must still comply with TAS.
accessibility.quote: If your project's total estimated cost is less than $50,000.00, you are not required to submit the project to the Department for registration and review, however, the project is still required to comply with TAS. Projects with costs of $50,000 or more are required to submit a full set of construction documents in accordance with Administrative Rule 68.50.
accessibility.city_note: Houston's adopted-codes list sends accessibility questions to TDLR: 'For regulations pertaining to Accessibility, please contact: Texas Department of Licensing & Regulation, Compliance - Architectural Barriers' (https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/media/2001/download).

permit_related_rule.quote: Any alteration, repair, remodel, renovation, or new construction in both residential and commercial buildings requires permits unless specifically exempted by the applicable code.
permit_related_rule.second_quote: Permits are not required for the following: ... Minor repair and maintenance of existing structures that include: (1) Painting, tarping, wallpapering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, and counter tops repair and replacement and similar finish work
permit_related_rule.note: Neither page names toilet partitions, so whether a like-for-like replacement counts as 'similar finish work' is a question for the city. The plan review page also says 'A commercial minor repairs permit is required for repairs that involve the replacement and/or repair of existing structural members and other building elements.'

delivery_note.note: A curb parking rule, not a truck ban. No Houston downtown truck-hours restriction was found on an official page.

accessibility.name: California Building Code Chapter 11B (accessibility for public buildings, public accommodations and commercial buildings)
accessibility.edition: 2025 CBC, enforced as part of the 2026 LABC
accessibility.authority: LADBS (plan check, Disabled Access); state standard written by the Division of the State Architect
accessibility.summary: Besides the 2010 ADA Standards, CBC Chapter 11B applies. Alterations trigger path-of-travel upgrades, including the toilet facilities serving the altered area; below the annual valuation threshold ($209,208 as of January 2026) the upgrade obligation is limited.
accessibility.quote: Where only toilet compartments are provided, at least 5 percent but no fewer than one toilet compartment shall comply with Section 11B-604.8.1.
accessibility.second_quote: Verify the project adjusted construction cost. If below the current valuation threshold (As of Jan 2026: $209,208*) and not all elements are proposed to be improved to comply with disabled access requirements, complete the "Summary of Upgrades Form" and detail path of travel improvements as required. (11B-202.4 Exception 8)

permit_related_rule.quote: 91.106.2. Work exempt from a permit. ... Permits shall not be required for the following: 1. Work regulated by this Code that is valued at $2,500 or less, unless it impacts the structural stability of a building, affects public safety, is performed to comply with a Department order, or involves a change in the use or occupancy. ... 15. Cases, counters and partitions, not over 5 feet 9 inches high.
permit_related_rule.note: The code exempts 'partitions, not over 5 feet 9 inches high' and work valued at $2,500 or less, but no LADBS page says whether toilet compartments count as such partitions (installed toilet partitions usually top out above 5 ft 9 in). Do not publish a yes/no without LADBS confirming.

building_code.quote: Effective December 31, 2023, the applicable codes in the State of Florida are: ... Florida Building Code- Building / 8th Edition (2023)
building_code.second_quote: The 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code takes effect December 31, 2026. To keep your master plans or stand-alone permit plans under the 8th Edition (2023), your project must achieve Plan Acceptance on or before December 30, 2026.

permit_related_rule.quote: Movable interior fixtures: Placing or repositioning free-standing shelves, clothing racks, or partitions that are not fixed to the structure and are no taller than 5 feet 9 inches.
permit_related_rule.second_quote: When in doubt, always check with the Building Department before starting work.
permit_related_rule.note: The city's no-permit list (Section 10-5 of the City of Miami Code) only covers partitions 'not fixed to the structure'. Toilet partitions are anchored, so they are not on the list, but the page does not say outright that they need a permit. Cabinet and countertop replacement is exempt for single-family homes and duplexes only.

accessibility.name: ICC A117.1-2017 with Washington amendments, through Chapter 11 of the Washington State Building Code (WAC 51-50) and Chapter 11 of the Seattle Building Code
accessibility.authority: Washington State Building Code Council (rule); SDCI (enforcement in Seattle)
accessibility.summary: Besides the 2010 ADA Standards, Washington adopts IBC Chapter 11 with ICC A117.1-2017 and its own amendments; Seattle enforces it through Chapter 11 of the Seattle Building Code.
accessibility.quote: Chapter 11 and other International Building Code requirements for barrier-free access, including ICC A117.1-2017 and Appendix E, are adopted pursuant to chapters 70.92 and 19.27 RCW.
accessibility.second_quote: Buildings and facilities shall be designed and constructed to be accessible in accordance with this code and ICC A117.1, except those portions of ICC A117.1 amended by this section.

permit_related_rule.quote: You don't need a permit for minor repairs or alterations that cost $6,000 or less in any 6-month period. The $6,000 limit is based on fair market value of labor and parts, even if you do the work yourself.
permit_related_rule.second_quote: You need a permit for any work on load-bearing supports, changes to the building envelope, and work that reduces egress, light, ventilation, or fire resistance no matter how small the project.
permit_related_rule.note: SDCI's page does not name toilet partitions; the full list is Seattle Building Code Section 106.2. A partition replacement above $6,000 (labor and parts) would not fit this exemption on its face.

delivery_note.text: Inside Seattle's Downtown Traffic Control Zone, trucks 30 feet or longer may not move during the weekday curfews (6-9 a.m. and 3-7 p.m.) and need an SDOT permit from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.; no permit is needed from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m., and nothing applies on Sundays.
delivery_note.quote: Vehicles 30 feet long and longer may move with a Downtown Traffic Control Zone permit from 9 AM – 3 PM, and from 7 PM – 6 AM without permit. Curfews shall be in effect from 6 – 9 AM and 3 – 7 PM, except Saturdays and Sundays.
delivery_note.second_quote: Commercial Vehicle Permits are required to use these zones unless a commercial vehicle makes payment at the nearby pay station or payment by phone.
